title: unified-edge-to-cloud-prd-rollout-2028-04-18
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview:

This PRD and rollout playbook describes the product scope, requirements, design constraints, and step-by-step launch plan for the "Converged Edge-to-Cloud" inference offering. The goal is a single developer-facing package (API + runtime configuration + billing model) that allows customers to run Redwood inference consistently across lightweight edge appliances and the hosted/dedicated cloud surface with predictable SLAs and cost controls.

Why this project now:
- Increasing demand for latency-sensitive, privacy-preserving use cases (on-device scoring, kiosk assistants, regulated industrial inference).
- Customers want a single contract and SDK that abstracts runtime location while preserving SLOs and cost transparency.
- Competitive differentiation: ship a first-class hybrid experience with automated fallback, delta-model sync, and unified observability.

Scope (what's in):
1) API/SDK surface updates to support location hints (edge/preferred-region/fallback-policy).
2) Runtime packaging for validated edge appliances (NVIDIA Jetson Orin family, selected Intel/AMD servers with discrete GPUs, and lightweight CPU-only devices), including quantization profiles and preforked KV cache snapshots.
3) Hybrid cache coordinator integration to maintain prefix/KV coherency between edge caches and cloud caches.
4) Billing + metering rules for hybrid consumption (local compute credits, sync delta charges, and cloud fallback token billing).
5) Console UX for per-tenant edge fleet management, rollout controls, and fidelity knobs.
6) Observability and quality monitoring: edge telemetry ingestion, synthetic prompt set regression checks, and drift detection.

Out of scope (for Phase 1):
- Support for fully air-gapped on-prem appliance installs (handled in Private wave).
- Marketplace bundling or reseller pricing (handled by GTM in Phase 2).

Goals and success metrics (KPIs):
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency for edge-local requests <= 60ms for short completions (<128 tokens) on validated appliances.
- Availability: Fleet-level uptime for edge nodes >= 99.5% calendar-month.
- Cost delta: Average per-token cost for hybrid workloads competitive with cloud-only by <= 15% after local compute credits applied.
- Quality: No more than 1.5% regression in evaluation prompt-set for quantized variants deployed to edge compared to cloud baseline.
- Adoption: 10 paying customers with production edge deployments within 6 months of launch.

User stories (representative):
- As an ML engineer, I want to pin a model variant to run locally on kiosk hardware and fall back to cloud if local capacity is saturated.
- As a platform engineer, I want console controls to rollback fidelity settings for a set of devices by region.
- As a finance lead, I want clear monthly metering rows that separate local compute credits from cloud token billing for chargeback.

High-level requirements (must-have):
- RQ-01: SDK accepts location hints and fallback policy flags with input validation and documented defaults.
- RQ-02: Edge runtime image with validated quantization profiles for each supported model family and hardware profile.
- RQ-03: Delta sync protocol to update small model patches (<200MB) without full model replacement.
- RQ-04: Hybrid cache coordinator that guarantees eventual KV prefix consistency and TTL-based eviction policy tuned for edge capacity.
- RQ-05: Telemetry pipeline extension to tag edge-originated traces and expose token-level cost attribution.
- RQ-06: Billing rules engine update to support local compute credits, monthly device allowances, and on-demand fallback token charges.
- RQ-07: Console flows for fleet onboarding, per-device rollout groups, and canary controls (percent-based, geo-based, and tag-based).

Non-functional constraints and design constraints:
- Memory: Edge runtime must operate with a peak resident set <= 9GB for the baseline quantized variant on the target device class.
- Boot time: Local model serving process must be ready (accept queries) within 90s after appliance reboot.
- Security: All edge images must support disk encryption at rest and TLS1.3 mTLS to Redwood control plane. Key management must integrate with customer KMS in Private wave; for Phase 1 use Redwood-managed ephemeral keys with audit logging.
- Upgrade model: Rolling in-place updates preferred; fallback to blue-green for devices that support container orchestration.

Compatibility matrix (validated hardware/profiles):
| Hardware class | Model family | Quant profile | Expected P95 <128 tokens | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Jetson-Orin (NX) | LLaMA-like 7B | int8-q4 | 58ms | validated reference image v1.0 |
| Intel NUC (i7, 16GB) | Small LLMs (3B) | int8-q4 | 85ms | CPU-only baseline; recommend 2 threads per request |
| AWS Graviton (edge region) | 7B quantized | bf16-fp16 mix | 70ms | cloud-side instance; for hybrid testing only |

Design notes (key decisions and rationale):
- Use a delta-model sync instead of full pull to avoid network egress spikes and to enable rapid rollbacks.
- Implement a lightweight local controller (single binary) that handles routing: local -> cloud fallback -> queued local retry. This keeps the SDK surface minimal and avoids complex client-side logic.
- Favor quantization profiles that prioritize quality above raw throughput for Phase 1; provide an "aggressive-cost" profile in Phase 2.

API / SDK changes (example):
- New request fields (SDK v2.5+):
  - location_hint: ["edge-local", "region:us-west-2", "cloud-preferred"]
  - fallback_policy: {"mode": "immediate|queue|failover", "max_cloud_tokens": 5000}  # represented as JSON in SDK

Example usage (pseudo-code):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
resp = client.generate(
  model="rw-7b-q4-edge",
  prompt="Summarize the last 10 messages",
  location_hint="edge-local",
  fallback_policy={"mode":"immediate","max_cloud_tokens":2000}
)
```

Rolling launch plan (phased):
1) Alpha (internal + 2 customers) — 8 weeks
  - Deliver edge runtime v1 images for Jetson NX and NUC, SDK v2.5 beta, basic console fleet view.
  - Acceptance: internal synthetic suite and two pilot customers validated.
2) Private Beta (10 customers) — 12 weeks
  - Add telemetry ingestion for edge traces, cost attribution, and delta sync resiliency tests.
  - Onboard billing rules for compute credits and per-device allowances.
  - Acceptance: automated regression tests pass; customers complete standard onboarding checklist.
3) Public GA — 6 weeks after Beta (contingent on metrics)
  - Full console UX, documentation, runbooks, and sales collateral.
  - Tiered pricing and packaging available (see Pricing implications).

Canary and rollback controls:
- Canary knobs: percent rollout (1%, 5%, 25%), geo filter, device-tag filter.
- Health checks during canary: p95 latency, error rate, model-quality delta on synthetic prompts.
- Automatic rollback triggers: 2x increase in error-rate over baseline OR 3% absolute regression in quality checks OR sustained p95 > 2x target for 30 minutes.

Observability and quality guardrails:
- Synthetic prompt set: 500 prompts per customer partitioned by features (QA, instruction, multi-turn). Run locally and in cloud; track loss and answer similarity (ROUGE/BLEU or embedding-based cosine).
- Edge heartbeat: 60s cadence metric with last-seen and resource snapshot. Alert if offline > 10 minutes for > 2% of fleet.
- Cost dashboards: per-device, per-route, and aggregated monthly views with drilldowns to token-level attribution.

Billing and packaging implications (summary):
- Pricing primitives: monthly device allowance (credits), local compute credits (per-second or per-request), fallback cloud token usage (per-token rate).
- Example SKU: Edge Starter — up to 50 devices, 10k local compute credits/month, fallback at cloud rates + 10% admin fee.
- Finance requirement: must expose line-itemized export for chargeback and metered billing with invoice tagging for local vs cloud consumption.

Runbooks and day-2 ops (high level):
- Onboarding checklist (operator):
  1) Register tenant and enable Edge feature flag.
  2) Provision device certificate via console and verify mTLS handshake.
  3) Push initial model delta and validate sample prompts.
  4) Set rollout group and start 1% canary.
- Incident response playbook summary:
  - If fleet-level p95 > threshold: increase fallback to cloud for affected groups, notify SRE and product owner, open incident ticket with root-cause label "edge-performance".
  - If delta sync fails: hold rollout, serve from previous model snapshot, and engage build/release to repackage delta.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- SDK, runtime images, and console controls released to internal staging environment.
- End-to-end tests verifying: location hint routing, fallback behavior, delta sync, and telemetry tagging.
- Billing records generated for hybrid usage in a sandbox tenant and reconciled with Finance.
- Runbook and customer-facing docs drafted and peer-reviewed.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Edge device heterogeneity leads to inconsistent quality.
  - Mitigation: Validate a narrow set of reference appliances for Phase 1 and expose an "unsupported" warning in SDK.
- Risk: Network partitions cause heavy cloud fallback and cost spikes.
  - Mitigation: Default fallback policy for edge devices is backoff + queueing; provide cost-safes in console (per-device token caps).
- Risk: Model drift due to different quant profiles on edge.
  - Mitigation: Periodic quality sampling and rollback automation; ensure quant profile labels in model registry.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Product lead (overall): Maya Patel
- Eng owners: Runtime team (Amber Zhou), SDK/API (Noah Grant), Billing (Priya Shah)
- SRE/Infra: Omar Reyes
- Go-to-market: Anika Bose

Open questions (must resolve before Beta):
1) Final definition and granularity of "local compute credit" (per-second vs per-inference).
2) Whether to allow customer-managed KMS for key material in Phase 1 (security trade-offs).
3) Exact default fallback policy — immediate vs queued with bounded cloud token cap.

Appendix (examples and reference commands):
- Example device provisioning flow (CLI):
```
redwood device provision --tenant acme --device-id kiosk-42 --profile jetson-nx --cert-path ./kiosk-42.crt
```
- Example delta patch upload (CLI):
```
redwood models delta-upload --model rw-7b --patch ./rw-7b-patch-v1.2.delta --target-profile jetson-nx
```
- Reference test matrix location: confluence://product-docs/requirements/edge-validation-test-matrix (TBD)

Notes for go-forward (Phase 2 possibilities):
- Expand supported appliance list and introduce an aggressive cost profile.
- Allow fully air-gapped installs with customer-provided KMS.
- Integrate with Redwood Optimize to propose on-device fidelity knobs automatically based on workload patterns.
